answer: Require each agent to lock a refundable stake that grows with its reputation, like a vine that only thickens after seasons of honest work. New identities start in a narrow canyon of limited privileges and must earn trust through verified, useful tasks before wider access opens. A strong reputation signal then comes from sustained performance, not from creating many cheap accounts, so an attacker must pay the stake and time cost for every fake identity, making large-scale Sybil attacks unprofitable.
